title: 16 ChatGPT myths: how to use AI as a co-pilot, not an oracle
summary: Ruben debunks 16 common beliefs about ChatGPT: it doesn't know the whole internet, forgets beyond its context window, hallucinates, carries bias, and isn't private or free. His core stance: treat AI output as a first draft, pair it with human taste and experience, and verify everything. He also announces a paid weekly video tier because AI courses go obsolete in weeks.

principles.text: Treat every AI reply as a first draft: verify, cross-check, then polish.
principles.quote: Treat every reply as a first draft. Verify, cross‑check, then polish.

principles.text: AI plus human beats either alone, so use it as a co-pilot; taste and experience are the moat.
principles.quote: On every possible benchmark, AI + human beats both AI or human alone.

principles.text: AI predicts the next token, not the next fact; confidence is not truth, so check sources.
principles.quote: It predicts the next token, not the next fact. When the data gap is big, it fills the void with fiction.

principles.text: Prompt specifically to pull the right knowledge: role framing makes answers instantly better.
principles.quote: if you say "Act like a data engineer", ChatGPT will directly go to its "data engineer database". The answer will be instantly better.

principles.text: Use multiple prompts and perspectives to detect AI bias and blind spots.
principles.quote: Use multiple prompts and perspectives to detect blind spots.

principles.text: AI course content goes stale fast, so ship weekly deep dives instead of static courses.
principles.quote: Because any AI course becomes obsolete… in 2 weeks.
